title: Digestive system
examples: Where does most of the nutrient absorption happen?
What is the job of enzymes in digestion?
How do villi help the body absorb food?

explain.say: The digestive system has many important organs working together. These organs break down the food we eat.
Now let me show you the real thing in 3D: the digestive system. Look at the oesophagus, the liver and the gall bladder. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.
Enzymes are special proteins that help speed up digestion. They break large food molecules into smaller ones.
Absorption is when the small, usable nutrients pass from the gut into the bloodstream. This moves energy to our body cells.
The small intestine has tiny finger-like projections called villi. These greatly increase the surface area for absorption.
For a real-life example, think about eating a sandwich. Enzymes in your mouth start breaking down the starch in the bread.
The most common mistake is thinking digestion only happens in the stomach. Remember, the small intestine is where most absorption occurs.

faq.q: Where exactly does the chemical digestion of carbohydrates start?
faq.a: It starts in the mouth because salivary amylase begins breaking down starches. You might also ask where amylase works or what breaks down starch.
asks: What is the first step in breaking down carbs?
Can digestion start before the stomach?

faq.q: Are all enzymes the same in the body?
faq.a: No, different enzymes are needed for different types of food. For example, one enzyme handles fats, and another handles proteins. You could also ask what digests fats or what enzyme digests protein.
asks: What breaks down fats in the gut?
Do we need different enzymes for different foods?

faq.q: What is the main purpose of the villi in the small intestine?
faq.a: Their main purpose is to increase the surface area so that nutrients can be absorbed quickly. This large area helps move energy into the blood. You could also ask how absorption is maximized or what the small intestine looks like.
asks: Why are the villi shaped like fingers?
How does the small intestine absorb nutrients?

faq.q: What happens to food after it leaves the small intestine?
faq.a: The remaining waste moves into the large intestine. Here, water is absorbed back into the body before the waste leaves the body. You might ask what happens in the large intestine or what the final waste product is.
asks: What is the function of the large intestine?

faq.q: Do we digest all the food we eat?
faq.a: No, some parts of the food, like fibre, are not broken down by human enzymes. This fibre passes through the system as waste. You could also ask what fibre does or if we digest everything.

facts: Digestion involves breaking food into small molecules.
Enzymes are biological catalysts that speed up reactions.
The small intestine has villi to increase surface area.
Absorption moves digested nutrients into the bloodstream.

quiz.say: Which organ is the primary site for nutrient absorption?
quiz.why: The small intestine is specifically structured with villi to maximize nutrient uptake.

wrong.0: The mouth only starts the breakdown of starches, not all nutrients.
wrong.1: The stomach primarily digests proteins, but most absorption happens later.
wrong.2: The large intestine mainly absorbs water, not the main nutrients.

quiz.say: If an enzyme is missing, what process will be most affected?
quiz.why: Enzymes are necessary to chemically break down large food molecules into absorbable parts.

wrong.0: Waste removal is the final step, which happens regardless of enzyme function.
wrong.2: Absorption is the movement across the wall, which happens even if digestion is slow.
wrong.3: Peristalsis is the muscle movement, which works even if enzymes are missing.

quiz.say: Which structure increases the surface area for absorption?
quiz.why: Villi are finger-like projections lining the small intestine, increasing the area for nutrient exchange.

wrong.0: The large intestine surface is not as specialized for nutrient absorption as the small intestine.
wrong.1: An enzyme is a chemical helper, not a physical surface structure.
wrong.3: The stomach lining is designed for acid and protein digestion, not maximum absorption.
